findings.claim: Inverted guard: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` then `Add` is the opposite of the other three hunks (`!ContainsKey`). When the key already exists, Add throws ArgumentException, which crashes the generator/analyzer for duplicate string keys. When the key is new, the member is never added, so string-keyed members are silently dropped from the TypeCollector's model. Any generated formatter then omits those members from serialization, which causes silent data loss, and deserialization skips them. The exception can also disable analyzer diagnostics (including the MsgPack00x protections) for the whole compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test for a [MessagePackObject(true)] or string-keyed type with a few [Key("a")] members in the second code path (hunk near line 1176). Run it and expect the generated formatter to contain all members. At head the members are missing; with duplicate keys, an ArgumentException is thrown. Also run existing generator snapshot tests via regeneration.
